title: OKR Orchestra: Conductor and Contingency Hedge for Cross-Functional Initiatives
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: company-level OKRs often become a laundry list of initiatives with unclear handoffs and brittle rollback behavior when priorities shift. Goal: build a lightweight coordination layer (the 'OKR Orchestra') that provides a single source of truth for cross-functional initiative state, a decision-reserve (contingency) for rebalancing capacity, and explicit rollback windows to minimize delivery chaos. We will produce a simple alignment matrix, decision playbook, and a lightweight UI/Slack signals workflow for exec and team-level signals. This ticket scopes the PM work to define the orchestration model, acceptance criteria, communication patterns, and initial pilot with 3 initiatives across Eng, Console, and Dedicated teams.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Alignment matrix prototype (owners, milestones, soft SLOs, rollback window) documented in Confluence and reviewed by Eng/Design/Sales
A2: Decision-reserve policy defined (how much capacity is tagged as contingency per quarter and rules for consumption)
A3: Playbook for triggering rollback (roles, timing, automated notifications) with two simulated runbooks tested
A4: Pilot dashboard wireframe showing initiative health, remaining contingency, and top-3 risks vetted by Console team
A5: Pilot executed on 3 initiatives with post-pilot retrospective and clear go/no-go recommendation for Q3 rollout
tasks: Task 1: Draft alignment matrix schema and fields (owner, milestones, SLOs, dependencies, contingency allocation)
Task 2: Convene working group (PM, Eng leads, Design, Ops) and run 2 workshops to map current initiatives
Task 3: Define contingency consumption rules and approval workflow
Task 4: Create Confluence playbook and Slack templates for escalation/rollback
Task 5: Build pilot dashboard wireframe and hand off to Console design
Task 6: Run pilot for 6 weeks, capture metrics and retro notes
success_metrics: SM1: 90% of pilot initiatives can be mapped into the alignment matrix within 2 working sessions
SM2: Contingency consumption requests processed within 48 hours during pilot
SM3: Reduction in ad-hoc priority-change incidents impacting SLOs by 30% in pilot slice
SM4: Stakeholder satisfaction score >= 4/5 in post-pilot survey
risks: R1: Teams may treat contingency as a slush fund and over-consume without tightening approval rules
R2: Tooling lag (dashboard + notifications) could hinder real-time decisions during the pilot
R3: Misaligned definitions of 'rollback' across teams could cause governance friction
